description: §4.12.5 + §23.4 - a nested `<program name= lang=>` with NO `use foreign:` in the parent. It is a FOREIGN LANGUAGE SIDECAR whether or not it also declares `port=`, so it emits no `new Worker(...)` and no worker bundle; pre-fix (S356) the §23.4 carve-out that suppressed the bogus worker keyed on `port=` ALONE, so this `port=`-less spelling of the same execution context was still compiled as a §4.12.4 web worker and shipped a 24-byte stub bundle. EXPECTATION HISTORY. r2: this case asserted E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL ABSENT, on the reasoning that §23.4 already fails the sidecar closed at the `use foreign:name { ... }` site — which is no reasoning at all for a file that has no such site, so the shape compiled exit 0 with its body silently discarded. r3: corrected to the code below, but made the carve-out CONDITIONAL, which double-fired elsewhere. r4: the carve-out is GONE and `E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL` is RETIRED — all four unbuilt §4.12.3 contexts are refused at the DECLARATION, claimed or not, so this case and its sibling `foreign-sidecar-claimed` now assert the SAME code. That is the tell that the seam is gone: the pair no longer distinguishes anything. COVERAGE NOTE (S356 r3, still true): `conformance/run.ts:203` checks `notCodes` UNCONDITIONALLY, so a `notCodes` entry genuinely bites even with an empty `codes` list. What the harness CANNOT check is CARDINALITY (it is set-based, so a double fire of one code is invisible) or artifact presence. Those halves are covered by `compiler/tests/integration/nested-program-worker-artifact-emission.test.js` (the SIDECAR_APP fixture), `nested-program-execution-context-gate.test.js`, and `nested-program-sidecar-unclaimed.test.js`.
rationale: §4.12.3's table gives "Foreign language sidecar | `name=`, `lang=` (non-WASM language) | Subprocess with HTTP/socket" — `port=` is a sidecar CONFIGURATION attribute (§4.12.2: "Port number for sidecar HTTP/socket communication"), not the discriminator. §4.12.3 normative (S356): the inline-worker context is selected if and only if `name=` is present and `lang=`/`mode=`/`route=`/`db=`/`port=` are all absent. E-FOREIGN-010 does not fire because there is no `use foreign:` in this file at all — that code is about an unresolved REFERENCE, and there is no reference.
